module_title: Gupta Empire and Harsha - Founders and Key Rulers
introduction: The Gupta period is known as the 'Golden Age' of ancient India. During this time, art, science, and literature flourished tremendously. After the decline of the Gupta Empire, Harshavardhana attempted to reunite North India. In this level, we will understand the key rulers of these empires.

core_concepts.title: Foundation of the Gupta Empire
core_concepts.description: Sri Gupta founded the Gupta dynasty, but Chandragupta I (319 CE) is considered its 'real founder', who assumed the title of 'Maharajadhiraja'.

core_concepts.title: Military Campaigns of Samudragupta
core_concepts.description: Samudragupta was a great conqueror. Due to his extensive military campaigns, historian V.A. Smith called him the 'Napoleon of India'.

core_concepts.title: Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya)
core_concepts.description: He defeated the Shakas and assumed the title 'Vikramaditya'. His court was adorned with the 'Navaratnas' (Nine Gems, including Kalidasa), and the Chinese traveler Fa-Hien visited India during his reign.

core_concepts.title: Vardhana Dynasty and Harshavardhana
core_concepts.description: Harshavardhana ascended the throne in 606 CE. He shifted his capital from Thanesar to Kannauj and established a strong empire across North India.

core_concepts.title: Harsha's Era and Hiuen Tsang
core_concepts.description: During Harsha's reign, the famous Chinese traveler Hiuen Tsang visited India and provided a detailed account of Harsha's administration and society.

important_entities.name: Samudragupta
important_entities.significance: Expanded the empire by defeating rulers of Aryavarta (North) and Dakshinapatha (South).

important_entities.name: Chandragupta II
important_entities.significance: The pinnacle of the Golden Age and the arrival of Chinese traveler Fa-Hien.

important_entities.name: Harshavardhana
important_entities.key_fact: Most prominent ruler of the Vardhana dynasty
important_entities.significance: United North India making Kannauj his central capital.

important_entities.name: Hiuen Tsang
important_entities.significance: Provided the most authentic information about Harsha's reign.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Founder vs. Real Founder of the Gupta Dynasty
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often get confused. If asked just for the 'founder', the answer is 'Sri Gupta', but if asked for the 'real founder', the answer is 'Chandragupta I'.
Fa-Hien visited during Chandragupta II's time, whereas Hiuen Tsang visited during Harshavardhana's time. Do not mix them up.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: H for Harsha, H for Hiuen Tsang
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Hiuen Tsang visited during Harsha's period. The remaining one, Fa-Hien, visited during Chandragupta II's period.

exam_strategy_tips: Questions directly matching rulers with their titles (e.g., Vikramaditya, Napoleon of India) are frequently asked.
Clearly memorize the contemporary rulers during the visits of Fa-Hien and Hiuen Tsang.
